'''''Tradescantia ohiensis''''', commonly known as '''bluejacket'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TROH|taxon=Tradescantia ohiensis|accessdate=14 December 2015}}</ref> or '''Ohio spiderwort''', is an herbaceous plant species in the genus ''[[Tradescantia]]'' native to eastern and central [[North America]].  It is the most common and widely distributed species of ''Tradescantia'' in the [[United States]], where it can be found from [[Maine]] in the northeast, west to [[Minnesota]], and south to [[Texas]] and [[Florida]]. It also has a very small distribution in [[Canada]] in extreme southern [[Ontario]] near [[Windsor, Ontario|Windsor]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=270385 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031130502/http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=270385 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 31, 2019 |title=''Tradescantia ohiensis'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref><ref>{{BONAP|ref |genus=Tradescantia |species=ohiensis}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Turner |first=B.L. |date=December 2006 |title=Texas species of ''Tradescantia'' (Commelinaceae) |url=https://www.phytologia.org/uploads/2/3/4/2/23422706/turner883312-331tradescantia10-16-06wfigs.pdf |journal=Phytologia |volume=88 |number=3 |pages=312–331 |publisher=Texensis Publishing |doi=10.5962/bhl.part.10459 |issn=0031-9430}}</ref>

==Description==
Distinguishing features of the species include [[glaucous]] leaves and stems, leaves forming an acute angle with the stems, sepals with hairs lacking glands which are confined to the apex if present at all, and a relatively tall habit (up to about {{convert|115|cm|ftin|disp=or}}). Typical habitats for the plant include roadsides, along railroads, and in fields and thickets. Less typically it can occur in woods, and sometimes along streams. As with many species in the genus, it often forms [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]]s with related species where they co-occur. More specifically, at least nine different species are thought to be capable of forming hybrids with ''T. ohiensis''.<ref name=flora>{{eFloras|1|222000425|Tradescantia ohiensis |family=Commelinaceae |last=Faden |first=Robert}}</ref>

==Uses==
Ohio spiderwort has edible flowers and shoots. Flowers and stems can be eaten raw, while the leaves can be cooked. Leaves of the plant are mucilaginous and can be used to soothe insect bites in a similar way to aloe vera.<ref name="Florida wildflowers">{{cite web|author=<!-- not stated --> |date=2024-05-30 |title=Spiderwort |url=https://www.flawildflowers.org/flower-friday-tradescantia |website=Florida Wildflower Foundation |access-date=2026-06-10}}</ref>
